root_cause: GCC does not prove complete collector-enum dispatch or stable PGO flag state across the opaque serialization call.
source_review: CompleteArrayBufferSweeping assigns scope_id for each of the three declared GarbageCollector values before tracing and finishing the sweep. An inactive sweeper bypasses tracing.

The SharedFunctionInfo branch saves the tiering decision under profile_guided_optimization, clamps it only during serialization and restores it under the same flag. Instrumented bytecode is likewise temporarily replaced and restored.
CodeSerializer::SerializeGeneric creates ObjectSerializer and synchronously serializes the object graph. The reviewed serialization path does not execute JavaScript.

Node src/node.cc explicitly disables V8 flag freezing to expose setFlagsFromString. Flags must NOT be described as immutable. Node doc/api/v8.md warns that changing flags after VM startup can cause unpredictable behavior, crashes or data loss.

coverage.native_matrix: All three collectors, active/inactive sweep and repeated completion; six tiering decisions, PGO on/off, absent/uninstrumented/instrumented debug info. Verify serialized state and restored decision/bytecode.
coverage.native_modes: Release/debug, normally and under Valgrind. Both exact warnings reproduce; both memory runs have zero errors and all allocations freed.
coverage.javascript_matrix: Four fresh Node processes: PGO on/off and minor mark-sweep on/off. Cold/lazy/hot code caches round-trip; corrupted header and wrong source length are rejected. ArrayBuffer contents survive minor and major collection.

limits: The collector enum, complete sweep helper, tiering enum and SharedFunctionInfo branch are verbatim. Heap, handle, trace and serializer adapters model state transitions, not a full V8 heap.
The serializer qualification assumes a stable PGO setting during synchronous serialization. Concurrent runtime flag mutation is not covered and is not claimed safe.
Actual JavaScript checks exercise packaged Node code-cache and GC behavior; they do not prove all adapter paths execute in that binary.

An initial control header link error was fixed before qualification. Two initial JavaScript negative tests hit the in-memory compilation cache; distinct script filenames now force the external-cache validation path without disabling compiler features.
No runtime patch, suppression or compiler-flag change is proposed.
